newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syrian paper condemns U.S. stand over arms deal.
newsitem.headline: Syrian paper condemns U.S. stand over arms deal.

text.p: An official Syrian newspaper on Wednesday implicitly condemned the United States for trying to block a South African arms deal with Damascus, saying the weapons would be defensive.
The Tishreen daily rejected Washington's charge that Syria was sponsoring terrorism and said Israel was using U.S. arms and economic aid to "terrorise Arabs and undermine peace".

"Everybody knows that Israel sees the flow of arms and aid to the Jewish state as an enouragement to it to continue its aggressive policy, reject the peace process, and conduct the ugliest types of terrorism..," Tishreen said.
"This forces Arab states to search for arms to defend their peoples and nations, and to confront the increasing Israeli threats and expansionist plans," it said.
Washington on Monday warned it might be forced to cut U.S. aid to South Africa if Pretoria follows through with plans to sell Syria $641 million in tank-gun aiming gear.
South African President Nelson Mandela's spokesman Parks Mankahlana responded by rejecting the U.S. warning and accusing Washington of high-handed bullying.
South Africa's department of foreign affairs later issued a statement that took a more conciliatory line saying no final decision was made on the deal so far.

U.S. state department spokesman Nicholas Burns on Tuesday said Washington would not make a decision on possibly reducing aid to South Africa until it acquired more facts on Pretoria's plans to sell arms to Syria.
